title: Diurna
description: The world, every day, in three sentences.

items.title: In Shenzhen, Trump sits down with Putin before a first three-way summit with Xi Jinping
items.content_html:
The American president met his Russian counterpart on Thursday morning on the sidelines of the APEC summit, a day after Xi Jinping greeted him on the tarmac. The three-way meeting is due to cover nuclear arms and the war with Iran.

Donald Trump held talks with Vladimir Putin on Thursday November 19th on the sidelines of the 33rd APEC leaders’ summit in Shenzhen, insisting that "wonderful" things could come of it and announcing a second meeting later in the day, according to India’s ANI news agency. The first three-way meeting with Xi Jinping is meant to cover cuts to nuclear arsenals, after the New START treaty lapsed in February, and the war with Iran, the White House told Al Jazeera, while Ukraine is not officially on the agenda. Greeted at the foot of his plane on Wednesday by the Chinese leader, a break with protocol, the American president arrives at a summit from which analysts quoted by Al Jazeera expect little of substance, with the academic Vuk Vuksanovic calling it a far cry from a new Yalta.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Iran claims an attack on a base in Kuwait as ships are hit near Hormuz
items.content_html:
Iran’s army says it targeted the Ali Al Salem base in Kuwait on Wednesday in retaliation for the American strike on Qeshm. A vessel belonging to the Emirati firm Adnoc was attacked off Oman, leaving 11 injured and one missing.

Iran’s army said on Wednesday November 18th that its drones had targeted Patriot air-defence batteries at the Ali Al Salem base in Kuwait, which hosts American forces, in retaliation for Washington’s strike the day before on a missile site on Qeshm island, according to Press TV, quoted by ABC News. Washington has not confirmed the claims; meanwhile Iran’s navy says three tankers caught fire after hitting mines east of the Strait of Hormuz, and Adnoc’s shipping arm reports 11 injured and one missing aboard one of its vessels, attacked off Oman on Tuesday night. The head of Iran’s army, General Amir Hatami, promises a response "without geographical limits" to any further American action, while Riyadh and Abu Dhabi have condemned the attacks and Bahrain is calling for action by the Security Council, on the eve of the Shenzhen summit.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Russian strikes kill four in Odesa as Brussels offers Kyiv a €45bn loan
items.content_html:
Russian strikes hit Odesa’s historic centre, part of it a UNESCO World Heritage site, on Wednesday, killing at least four people. The European Commission is proposing a €45bn loan for next year.

At least four people were killed and 13 injured in Odesa on Wednesday November 18th when three Russian strikes hit the historic centre, including a UNESCO-protected area, according to local officials, with Volodymyr Zelensky accusing Moscow of striking again after rescuers arrived. The same day the European Commission proposed a €45bn loan to cover part of a financing gap put at €70bn for next year, to be repaid only once Russia has paid reparations, according to its president, Ursula von der Leyen. Overnight Ukrainian forces struck the Crimean bridge again, where rail traffic was suspended according to Russia’s transport ministry, while the coalition of the willing meets in Berlin on Thursday to discuss air defence and energy.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: At COP31 in Antalya, phasing out fossil fuels divides delegates two days before the close
items.content_html:
The draft deal published on Monday offers two options on fossil fuels, one of them an outright phase-out. The European Union wants major changes, and the conference is due to end on Friday.

Some 200 countries gathered in Antalya, Turkey, for COP31 are haggling over an 18-page draft decision published on Monday November 16th, which offers two options on fossil fuels: the transition away from them agreed in 2023, or an outright phase-out. The EU’s climate commissioner, Wopke Hoekstra, says the text needs a thorough overhaul, while dozens of European, African and Pacific states that want the next IPCC report before COP33 are up against a bloc that includes Saudi Arabia and India. Australia’s minister, Chris Bowen, who is leading the negotiations under a presidency shared with Turkey, admitted that some clauses had already been rejected and promised at least one new draft before the close, due on Friday November 20th, though COPs often overrun.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: On the Ethiopia-Eritrea border, the two armies mass around Badme
items.content_html:
According to conflict monitors and sources close to Tigrayan militias, Addis Ababa and Asmara have concentrated forces along their border. Fire has been exchanged near Badme, the flashpoint of the 1998-2000 war.

Ethiopia and Eritrea have massed forces along their shared border, according to the conflict monitor ACLED, the International Crisis Group and two sources close to Tigrayan militias quoted by Reuters on Wednesday November 18th, raising fears of open war between the neighbours. According to ACLED, Ethiopian drones struck probable Eritrean positions around Badme on November 12th, Eritrea answered with artillery and the two armies clashed on the Ethiopian side the next day, the first direct exchanges in more than a month, which Reuters could not confirm. Eritrea’s information minister, Yemane Gebremeskel, decries "propaganda" from Addis Ababa’s ruling party, which has not responded, while Magnus Taylor, an analyst at the International Crisis Group, fears that fighting against Tigrayan rebels could drag the two countries into direct conflict.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: America strikes an Iranian missile site on Qeshm as drones target Kuwait
items.content_html:
A US official says the military hit a missile-launch site on the island of Qeshm on Tuesday evening, in retaliation for Iran’s attack on a base in Bahrain. Overnight, Kuwait said it was intercepting "hostile" drones.

American forces struck a missile-launch site on the Iranian island of Qeshm, in the Strait of Hormuz, on the evening of Tuesday 17 November, according to a US official quoted by Al Jazeera, hours after the Revolutionary Guards claimed a drone attack on a radar at Sheikh Isa air base in Bahrain. The deputy governor of Hormozgan province, Ahmad Nafisi, insists that no homes or businesses were hit, while US Central Command says the drones launched at Bahrain, in the third Iranian attack on the kingdom in five days, were intercepted without causing damage. Overnight Kuwait’s army said it was repelling "hostile" drone attacks without saying where they came from, and Manama condemned Iran’s "criminal attacks", on the eve of the Shenzhen summit at which Washington wants to raise the war with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Putin arrives in Shenzhen ahead of his first three-way summit with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping
items.content_html:
Russia’s president landed in Shenzhen on Tuesday and is due to hold talks with Xi Jinping on Wednesday before Thursday’s three-way meeting with Donald Trump. The American president flies on to China after a state visit to Manila on Wednesday.

Vladimir Putin landed at Shenzhen’s Bao’an airport on Tuesday 17 November for his first APEC summit in person since 2017, and is due to meet Xi Jinping on Wednesday ahead of the first three-way meeting with Donald Trump, scheduled for Thursday on the sidelines of the summit. Washington wants to discuss cutting nuclear arsenals, since the last Russian-American nuclear-arms treaty expired in February, as well as the Iran war, while Ukraine’s place on the agenda remains unclear, Donald Trump having said on Monday that he would raise it despite signals to the contrary from the White House. Before leaving the Philippines, the American president was received on Wednesday for a state visit by Ferdinand Marcos Jr at Malacañang Palace, where he said he was "not concerned" about tensions in the South China Sea, and he has not ruled out seeing Kim Jong Un in China.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Board of Peace warns that the Gaza ceasefire is at risk of collapse
items.content_html:
In a report delivered to the UN Security Council on Tuesday, the body overseeing the truce accuses Israel of blocking the transitional civilian administration. It argues that a ceasefire producing "nothing visible" cannot last indefinitely.

The Board of Peace, set up in 2025 at Donald Trump’s initiative to oversee the truce between Israel and Hamas, delivered a report to the United Nations Security Council on Tuesday 17 November warning that the deal risks collapse unless it is implemented immediately, according to the Associated Press. The document accuses Israel of preventing the technocratic civilian administration from taking office in Gaza and of failing to decide on the return of a civilian police force, which is delaying the international stabilisation force, and also cites Israeli strikes and Hamas’s military activity. It asks the Security Council to press both sides, warns that if the plan fails there is "no alternative roadmap", and calls for shelters and winter supplies to be let in on a large scale for a population facing "another winter in tents".

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Ukraine launches a record drone attack on Russia, hitting a refinery in Bashkortostan
items.content_html:
Moscow says it intercepted 1,441 Ukrainian drones overnight from Monday to Tuesday, a record since 2022. Fires were reported at a Gazprom petrochemical complex in Salavat, and an arch of the Crimean bridge has collapsed.

Russia’s defence ministry said on Tuesday 17 November that it had intercepted 1,441 Ukrainian drones overnight over Russia and annexed Crimea, a record since the invasion began that eclipses the 1,336 claimed the previous night. Fires were reported at the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat complex in Bashkortostan, more than 1,200 kilometres from the border, which regional authorities say is intact, while Ukraine’s security service claims to have destroyed a road arch of the Crimean bridge in a seven-stage operation. The same night, Russian missiles hit Kyiv’s North and South bridges and energy facilities, cutting power in eight regions according to the deputy energy minister, Artem Nekrasov, two days before a summit in Shenzhen at which the war’s place remains uncertain.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: UN counts more than 4,500 killed in Haiti’s gang violence since January
items.content_html:
The UN human rights office recorded 4,595 deaths between January and October and urges the forces fighting the gangs to limit their use of lethal force. In Port-au-Prince, hundreds of people marched in support of Salvadoran troops.

The UN human rights office said in Geneva on Tuesday 17 November that 4,595 people had been killed and 2,050 wounded in Haiti between 1 January and 31 October, including at least 514 killed in security-force operations against gangs between July and September. The high commissioner, Volker Türk, urged national and international forces, including the UN-authorised Gang Suppression Force, to use lethal force only when "unavoidable", as El Salvador has deployed more than 2,000 troops since October, mostly outside that framework. Hundreds of Haitians marched on Tuesday, notably in Port-au-Prince, in support of the deployment, which San Salvador says will end once four Salvadorans abducted on 18 October are found; the leader of the 400 Mawozo gang, Wilson Joseph, claims without evidence that they have been killed.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Iran says it targeted an American radar in Bahrain as more tankers burn in Hormuz
items.content_html:
The Revolutionary Guards say they struck at a radar at Bahrain’s Sheikh Isa base on Tuesday; Bahrain says it intercepted the attack. Iran’s navy reports three more tankers ablaze after striking mines.

The Revolutionary Guards claimed on Tuesday 17 November to have targeted the American radar system at Sheikh Isa base in Bahrain, home to the US Fifth Fleet, whose authorities said they intercepted the attack without casualties or damage, while Iran’s navy reported three tankers ablaze after hitting mines since the morning. These claims cannot be verified, but Britain’s maritime agency, UKMTO, reported another attack on a tanker north of Khasab, in Oman, whose crew was reported missing, and an Iranian official blamed America for an explosion on Qeshm island, which he said caused no damage. Donald Trump, who says he may hold off attacking Iran depending on Tehran’s conduct, warned that Iran would "pay a price" for threats against Washington, as the foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, visited Oman and Qatari and Iranian officials met.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: In Yemen, the Houthis close in on Aden after pro-government forces pull back from Bab al-Mandeb
items.content_html:
Saudi-backed forces have abandoned the coast near the Bab al-Mandeb strait to defend Aden, which the Houthis are now approaching to within about 60 kilometres. On Monday King Salman dismissed the commander of Saudi Arabia’s joint forces.

Yemen’s pro-government forces announced on Sunday 15 November that they had withdrawn from Dhubab airport and from their positions near the Bab al-Mandeb strait to fall back on Aden, seat of the internationally recognised government, and the Houthis promptly followed, coming to within about 60 kilometres north of the city. The retreat, which the armed forces’ spokesman called a redeployment, costs the coalition one shore of a strait that has carried Saudi oil exports since Hormuz was all but closed, and on Monday King Salman dismissed, without explanation, the commander of the joint forces, General Fahd bin Hamad al-Salman. The Houthis have fired drones towards the Mecca and Riyadh regions, which Saudi Arabia says it shot down, while in besieged Taiz the authorities are calling for humanitarian corridors and doctors fear hospitals will shut down for lack of fuel and oxygen.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Donald Trump lands in Manila for the close of the ASEAN summit, before heading to Shenzhen
items.content_html:
The American president arrived in Manila on Tuesday, on the final day of the 49th ASEAN summit, and convened the Quad’s leaders for the first time in his second term. He then travels on to Shenzhen for APEC.

Donald Trump landed in Manila at 5.33pm local time on Tuesday 17 November, accompanied among others by the secretary of state, Marco Rubio, as the 49th ASEAN summit drew to a close and the Philippines handed the bloc’s chairmanship to Singapore for 2027. He promptly convened the Quad with the prime ministers of Australia, Anthony Albanese, Japan, Sanae Takaichi, and India, Narendra Modi, a first since his return to the White House, which announced work on artificial intelligence and a joint exercise for maritime patrol aircraft. On the sidelines, Washington and Bangkok signed a trade statement under which Thailand would scrap its tariffs on American goods, ahead of an official welcome by Ferdinand Marcos Jr on Wednesday and Mr Trump’s departure for APEC in Shenzhen.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: A section of the Crimean bridge collapses as Russia strikes Kyiv’s bridges
items.content_html:
A fresh Ukrainian strike overnight brought down a road span of the Kerch bridge, now closed to traffic. In Kyiv, Russian missiles hit two bridges and cut water and heating to some districts.

The Kerch bridge, the only direct link between Russia and annexed Crimea, was struck overnight from 16 to 17 November for the second time in 24 hours, and Ukraine’s general staff says an arch and a span of the road section have collapsed. Russia’s transport ministry suspended road and rail traffic and said there were no casualties, while in Kyiv the mayor, Vitali Klitschko, said Russian missiles had hit the North and South bridges, cutting water and heating to some districts. The strikes come as several European ministers say it is premature to discuss the continent’s security with Moscow before a ceasefire, and two days before Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping are due to meet.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: In Myanmar, an air strike kills 12 displaced people in Rakhine as ASEAN keeps Min Aung Hlaing out
items.content_html:
An air strike blamed on the army killed 12 people in a camp for displaced people in Rakhine state, according to witnesses. Meeting in Manila, ASEAN leaders extended the ban on Myanmar’s president attending their summits.

An air strike killed 12 people, including a five-year-old child, and wounded 18 on the evening of Friday 13 November at the Byar La camp for displaced people in Ponnagyun township, north-east of Sittwe, according to witnesses and a rescue organisation quoted by AFP. Rakhine state, almost entirely controlled by the Arakan Army, is under an army blockade and regular air strikes, and the army could not be reached for comment, while the civil war that followed the 2021 coup has killed more than 100,000 people, according to ACLED. Meeting in Manila on Sunday, ASEAN leaders extended the ban on President Min Aung Hlaing attending their summits, citing a lack of progress on the 2021 peace plan, while raising the prospect of Myanmar’s representation being gradually restored under conditions.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Iran says six tankers have hit mines near Hormuz as a third American carrier arrives
items.content_html:
The Revolutionary Guards say six tankers have caught fire after striking mines near Hormuz since Sunday, a day after a claimed drone attack on Bahrain. A third American aircraft carrier has reached the region, and Tehran rules out any nuclear inspections until the war is over.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said on Monday 16 November that two more tankers had struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz, bringing to six the number of ships set ablaze since Sunday according to Iranian state media, a day after they claimed a six-drone attack on the Riffa base in Bahrain. The American carrier Theodore Roosevelt has arrived in the region, joining the George H. W. Bush and the George Washington, while a Panama-flagged tanker, the ON Phoenix, was hit by an unknown projectile off Oman without casualties, The Times of Israel reports. Kazem Gharibabadi, Iran’s deputy foreign minister, rules out any IAEA access to nuclear sites until the war has permanently ended, while Abbas Araghchi, the foreign minister, said in Islamabad that the Economic Cooperation Organisation backs an Iranian plan to reopen Hormuz within two days, on conditions.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Ukraine launches its biggest drone attack on Russia, reaching as far as the Crimean bridge
items.content_html:
Moscow says it intercepted 1,336 Ukrainian drones in one night, a record since the invasion began, nearly 600 of them heading for the Moscow region. The Kremlin reports “insignificant” damage to the Kerch bridge, while Kyiv presses for Starshield restrictions to be lifted.

Russia’s defence ministry said on Monday 16 November that it had intercepted 1,336 Ukrainian drones in a single night, the highest number it has claimed since the invasion, about 600 of them aimed at the Moscow region according to the city’s mayor, Sergei Sobyanin, the Associated Press reports. The Kerch bridge linking Crimea to Russia was targeted, with the Kremlin’s spokesman, Dmitry Peskov, describing the damage as “insignificant”, while Volodymyr Zelensky says Ukraine has knocked out more than 55% of Russia’s refining capacity and condemns the speed limits on SpaceX’s Starshield terminals. Russia fired more than 2,300 drones, 1,590 glide bombs and 15 missiles at Ukraine in a single week, according to Ukraine’s president, and its strikes on the Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk regions left hundreds of thousands of homes without power as winter approaches.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: ASEAN and China fail to conclude their code of conduct for the South China Sea
items.content_html:
Meeting in Manila, South-East Asian countries could not finish the text promised for 2026 with Beijing, though some 80% of it has been provisionally agreed. The Philippine chair hands the file to Singapore, before Donald Trump arrives on Tuesday.

The Philippines’ foreign secretary, Ma. Theresa Lazaro, acknowledged on Sunday 15 November, on the sidelines of the 49th ASEAN summit in Manila, that the bloc and China had not concluded a code of conduct for the South China Sea, despite provisional agreement on about 80% of the draft’s paragraphs, Reuters reports. Still unresolved are whether the text will be legally binding and what area it will cover, with Beijing claiming almost all of a sea through which half the world’s merchant ships pass, despite a 2016 arbitral ruling it rejects, against rival claims from the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei and Indonesia. Singapore, which takes over the ASEAN chair next year, inherits a text that has been under negotiation for more than two decades, while Donald Trump is due in Manila on Tuesday for a special ASEAN-US summit before heading to Shenzhen for APEC.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.
tags: Tensions in the South China Sea

items.title: Halfway through COP31, climate finance still divides rich and developing countries
items.content_html:
The developing countries’ bloc rejected a text on climate finance as too weak in Antalya on Saturday, just as ministers take over from negotiators. The coalition to move away from fossil fuels presses on without Colombia, one of its founders.

The Group of 77 and China on Saturday 14 November rejected in Antalya the latest text on the work programme for climate finance, calling it too weak, as COP31 enters its second week with the arrival of ministers, according to Climate Action Network. African countries have made tripling adaptation finance to at least $120bn a year by 2035 their priority, but the European Union, Japan and Norway object to that benchmark, while the mechanism for a just transition amounts, for now, to a knowledge centre and an annual meeting. Simon Stiell, the UN’s climate chief, calls progress “constructive” and urges delegations to avoid stalling tactics before the scheduled close on Friday, while the coalition launched in Santa Marta to move away from fossil fuels carries on without Colombia, which left it after Abelardo de la Espriella’s election.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: In Sudan, the army regains ground in Kordofan, where drone strikes are killing civilians
items.content_html:
Sudan’s army and its Darfuri allies have retaken several towns in West Kordofan and loosened the grip on El Obeid. Civilians are paying the price of the offensive, caught between drones and paramilitary attacks.

Sudan’s army and allied Darfuri forces have in recent days retaken several strategic towns in West Kordofan, including Al-Khuwei, breaking the siege that the Rapid Support Forces had imposed on El Obeid, the capital of North Kordofan, according to Al Jazeera. General Hemedti’s paramilitaries still hold En Nahud, a gold-mining town where they have killed ten civilians since Thursday, according to a local relief group quoted by Anadolu, while drone strikes have killed at least 15 civilians in the region in recent days, according to the Sudanese outlet Darfur24. Analysts quoted by Al Jazeera expect the paramilitaries to fall back towards Darfur, their tribal heartland, as the UN describes Kordofan as the epicentre of the conflict and most humanitarian operations there have been suspended.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: America floats NATO membership for Ukraine in exchange for a withdrawal from the Donbas
items.content_html:
According to Volodymyr Zelensky, American negotiators have for the first time linked his country’s accession to the Atlantic alliance to giving up the parts of the Donbas that Kyiv still holds. Ukraine’s president rejects any cession of territory, but says he is ready to consult Ukrainians if offered a complete package of guarantees.

In remarks released by his office on Saturday 14 November, Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelensky, said American negotiators had asked him whether Ukraine would withdraw from the Donbas in exchange for NATO membership, the first time, in his account, that the alliance has been tied to territorial concessions, Al Jazeera reports. The areas in question are those Russia does not control, and Mr Zelensky refused to give them up, while saying he would put the matter to a referendum if America and its allies offered security guarantees, a funded army and a reconstruction plan; Vladimir Putin regards Ukraine’s membership as a red line. Kyiv now awaits details: Washington talks of guarantees resembling Articles 4 and 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty, but with no American troops on Ukrainian soil, according to the Kyiv Independent, while the Europeans have chosen five countries to represent them in future negotiations.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Trump, Xi and Putin to meet in Shenzhen on Thursday for a first three-way nuclear summit
items.content_html:
The White House has confirmed an unprecedented meeting of the American, Chinese and Russian presidents on the sidelines of the APEC summit, focused on cutting nuclear arsenals. Washington expects no agreement, and Ukraine will not be on the agenda.

The White House’s deputy press secretary, Olivia Wales, announced on Friday 13 November that Donald Trump would meet Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on Thursday 19 November, on the sidelines of the APEC summit, to discuss reducing nuclear weapons worldwide, Al Jazeera reports. The New START treaty, which capped the Russian and American arsenals, expired in February after Mr Trump declined a one-year extension in order to demand a new deal that includes China, which argues that Washington and Moscow, with far bigger stockpiles, should negotiate between themselves. A senior American official warns that no agreement is expected and speaks of the start of a conversation, with the president due to raise the war with Iran but not Ukraine, while Volodymyr Zelensky fears a repeat of the Yalta conference and a carve-up into spheres of influence.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Netanyahu invokes the Iranian threat to demand a unity government as Washington bets on pressure
items.content_html:
Israel’s outgoing prime minister is urging Gadi Eisenkot to form a unity government with him capable of “eliminating” the Iranian threat, an offer his rival promptly rejected. American intelligence reckons Tehran still has thousands of missiles, while Washington sees no need for a fresh offensive.

In a video statement released on Saturday 14 November, Israel’s outgoing prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, called on Gadi Eisenkot, who has been asked to form the next government, to join him in a national-unity government to remove the Iranian threat “once and for all”, an offer Mr Eisenkot dismissed within minutes, Al Jazeera reports. The head of Mossad, Roman Gofman, met the CIA’s director, John Ratcliffe, in Washington to seek American backing for new strikes, according to Haaretz, just as the Wall Street Journal, citing American intelligence, estimated that Iran retains between 1,500 and 2,500 missiles despite the bombing. America’s secretary of state, Marco Rubio, has nonetheless said fresh military action is unnecessary because the economic pressure on Tehran is considerable, while the Knesset elects its speaker on Tuesday and Mr Eisenkot has 28 days, extendable by 14, to form a coalition.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: America loses its measles-elimination status after a string of outbreaks
items.content_html:
The Pan American Health Organisation has concluded that the virus is once again circulating continuously in America, a quarter of a century after it was eliminated. Experts blame falling childhood vaccination, while the administration blames its predecessors.

The Pan American Health Organisation (PAHO), the WHO’s regional arm, concluded this week that measles transmission had become established again in America, which thus loses its status as a country that has eliminated the disease, according to researchers quoted by KFF Health News, with an official announcement due on 17 November. Elimination requires every outbreak to die out within a year, which has no longer been the case since a cluster in Utah crossed that threshold in June, following the west Texas outbreak that infected more than 4,500 people in America and Mexico in 2025. Robert F. Kennedy Jr’s health department attributes the situation to vaccination gaps that predate the current administration, while former officials at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention say regaining elimination status is a distant prospect until the current outbreaks are contained.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.
tags: The return of measles in America

items.title: In Nigeria, diphtheria has killed more than 1,100 people this year and antitoxin is running out
items.content_html:
The worst diphtheria epidemic on record in the country has caused more than 28,000 confirmed cases, mostly among poorly vaccinated children. Médecins Sans Frontières warns that its stocks of the only effective treatment are “dangerously low”.

Médecins Sans Frontières warned on Friday 13 November that its stocks of diphtheria antitoxin were almost exhausted in northern Nigeria, where its teams are already rationing treatment, as the country has recorded 28,151 confirmed cases and 1,126 deaths since January, according to health authorities quoted by Premium Times. The epidemic, which emerged in late 2022, mainly strikes unvaccinated or under-vaccinated children in 26 states and the Federal Capital Territory, with Kano state alone accounting for 43% of confirmed cases, while global production of antitoxin remains limited and erratic. The charity is calling for higher global production, faster customs clearance for medicines and sustained investment in routine immunisation, as a new outbreak is reported at a boarding school of more than 2,000 pupils in Kano state, according to Anadolu.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Europe picks five countries for the Ukraine talks as Berlin warns Washington against surprises
items.content_html:
Meeting in Dublin, European leaders entrusted their voice in future negotiations to the EU’s institutions and to five members of the “coalition of the willing”. Germany’s chancellor has asked Donald Trump for “no surprises” ahead of his expected talks with Vladimir Putin in China.

On Friday 13 November, after a meeting of European leaders in Dublin, the president of the European Council, António Costa, announced that Europe would be represented at future negotiations on Ukraine by the EU and five members of the “coalition of the willing”: Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Poland, Al Jazeera reports. The choice answers America’s envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, the latter having urged Europe to speak with one voice, but Moscow still refuses to involve Europeans directly, with the Kremlin’s spokesman, Dmitry Peskov, insisting that no decision has been taken. Germany’s chancellor, Friedrich Merz, who expects Donald Trump to discuss Ukraine with Vladimir Putin in China next week, has asked the American president for “no surprises”, with some in Dublin fearing a “second Anchorage”, according to Reuters, quoted by Al-Monitor.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Qatar seals a defence pact with Turkey as Israel debates a strike on Iran
items.content_html:
Doha and Ankara pledged on Friday to stand together against any armed attack on either of them, a sign of waning faith in America’s guarantees in the Gulf. In Israel, Benjamin Netanyahu’s caretaker government is preparing a fresh offensive against Iran, without open backing from the army or Washington.

In Istanbul on Friday 13 November, Turkey’s president, Recep Tayyip Erdogan, and the emir of Qatar, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, signed a mutual-defence agreement under which the two countries promise a common stance against any external armed attack, Al Jazeera reports. Gulf monarchies believe America’s security guarantees no longer work, according to a Turkish analyst quoted by the channel, as the Revolutionary Guards’ navy says an LNG tanker struck a mine in Hormuz and America’s military command says it shot down two Iranian drones heading for Bahrain. In Israel, the security cabinet chaired by the outgoing prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, has ordered faster preparations for an attack on Iran, according to Israeli media, though the general staff sees no urgency and Gadi Eisenkot, who is tasked with forming the next government, fears “devastating” consequences.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: A telecoms failure grounds every flight in America for more than four hours
items.content_html:
The Federal Aviation Administration halted all take-offs nationwide on Friday after an outage hit air-traffic control centres. Thousands of flights were cancelled, and a return to normal could take several days.

At 3.54pm New York time on Friday 13 November, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) halted all departures nationwide, citing “extraordinary circumstances”, after a telecoms failure hit the en-route centres that control aircraft at altitude, Al Jazeera reports. According to the transport secretary, Sean Duffy, switches and routers overloaded with data gave way, without a total loss of communications or radar, and the homeland-security secretary, Markwayne Mullin, ruled out a cyber-attack. Airspace reopened at 8.15pm after more than four hours, but more than 4,700 flights were cancelled on Friday, according to FlightRadar24, and Mr Duffy, who wants $50bn to modernise air-traffic control, promises a return to normal before Thanksgiving.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: The Houthis step up strikes on Saudi Arabia as the UN extends sanctions on Yemen
items.content_html:
Riyadh says it intercepted drones over its capital and Eastern Province on Thursday, while Yemen’s rebels claim attacks on oil and military sites. The Security Council has renewed sanctions on Yemen for another year.

On Thursday 12 November the spokesman for the Saudi-led coalition, General Turki al-Maliki, announced the interception of drones over the Riyadh region and the Eastern Province, while the Houthis’ military spokesman, Yahya Saree, claimed strikes on a pipeline, the port of Yanbu and two military sites, Al Jazeera reports. The attacks target the main route around Hormuz, with Riyadh saying it pumps some 4m barrels of crude a day through the East-West pipeline to Yanbu on the Red Sea, while Yemen’s government forces have pressed an offensive against the rebels since October. On Thursday the Security Council unanimously extended for a year the asset freezes and travel bans targeting Yemen and condemned the Houthis’ escalation, while Riyadh is urging the European Union to add them to its list of terrorist organisations, according to Reuters.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: In Burkina Faso, rival jihadists fight each other while the state fails to regain ground
items.content_html:
Since September, Islamic State Sahel and the al-Qaeda-linked JNIM have fought each other with rare ferocity near the Malian border. The junta, which has lost control of vast areas, is meanwhile tightening its crackdown on critics.

Since early September, fighting between Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM), an al-Qaeda affiliate, and Islamic State Sahel has intensified in northern Burkina Faso along the border with Mali, with Islamic State’s weekly claiming more than 400 rival fighters killed on 9 October, Al Jazeera reports. The rivalry, which dates back to 2019, has already killed more than 2,200 fighters according to ACLED, a conflict monitor, and distracts JNIM from its war on the army, even as the group controls large swathes of the north, centre-north, west and east, according to the International Crisis Group. The junta of Captain Ibrahim Traoré, in power since September 2022, this month issued “terrorism” arrest warrants for some twenty people, including a journalist from RFI, while 4.5m people need humanitarian aid in 2026, according to the UN.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: In Dublin, Volodymyr Zelensky announces a record prisoner swap and Europe’s seat at the table
items.content_html:
Ukraine’s president says Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, whom he received on Thursday evening on their way back from the Kremlin, promised him the biggest prisoner exchange of the war. Europeans are expected to join the next round of talks, though Moscow has not confirmed it.

On the evening of Thursday 12 November, at Baldonnel air base west of Dublin, Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelensky, received America’s envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, a few hours after their meeting with Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin, the Kyiv Independent reports. Mr Zelensky says the meeting “unblocked” the three-way talks, paved the way for the largest exchange of prisoners of war since 2022 and secured direct European representation at the next session, with Mr Kushner arguing that no deal is possible without Europe, according to the Kyiv Post. No date has yet been set for the new round, whose format the Kremlin has not confirmed, while the “coalition of the willing” is due to meet in Berlin next week and EU leaders will weigh Kyiv’s financing needs for 2027 on 26-27 November.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Iran says it hit an American radar in Bahrain as Donald Trump rules out a deal
items.content_html:
The Revolutionary Guards claim to have destroyed an American early-warning radar in Bahrain on Friday in retaliation for a strike on the port of Sirik, a claim America’s military disputes. A day earlier America’s president called a deal with Tehran unnecessary and took his vice-president off the file.

On Thursday 12 November Donald Trump wrote that America did “not need a deal with Iran” and told his vice-president, JD Vance, who had been considering a meeting with the secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, Mohsen Rezaei, to focus on crime in Democratic-run cities, Middle East Eye reports. The reversal, days after he spoke of “momentum” towards a settlement, comes as Tehran denies any planned meeting in Qatar, refuses to send its enriched uranium abroad and keeps the Strait of Hormuz closed until its conditions are met. On Friday 13 November the Revolutionary Guards said they had destroyed an American early-warning radar in Bahrain in retaliation for an unclaimed strike on a telecoms tower in Sirik, on the Strait of Hormuz, while America’s Central Command says it shot down two drones, causing no damage, according to RFE/RL and Fox News.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Dogged by suspicions of Chinese espionage, Jensen Huang steps down as Nvidia’s boss
items.content_html:
The co-founder of the AI-chip giant resigned on Thursday, after revelations of an affair with a woman whom American officials suspect of spying for Beijing. The chief financial officer, Colette Kress, takes over in the interim.

On Thursday 12 November Nvidia announced the resignation “effective immediately” of its chief executive and co-founder, Jensen Huang, 63, who also leaves the board, gave no official reason and named its chief financial officer, Colette Kress, as interim boss, Al Jazeera and The National report. On 8 November he had admitted an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Megaspeed, a Singaporean firm, whom American officials suspect of spying for Beijing, while Nvidia, which controls about 90% of the market for advanced AI chips, sits at the heart of the Sino-American technology rivalry. The shares fell by more than 14% at one point on Thursday, the board, now chaired by Harvey Jones, is looking for a successor, and Republican lawmakers are threatening a subpoena to question Mr Huang about the affair’s implications for national security.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.
tags: Nvidia and the China spying claims

items.title: Spain’s first general strike since 2012 puts housing at the heart of the election
items.content_html:
Hundreds of thousands marched through Spain’s big cities on Wednesday, answering the main unions’ call to protest against soaring rents and for higher wages. The mobilisation comes less than three weeks before the snap general election of 29 November.

On Wednesday 11 November Spain held its first general strike since 2012, called by the CCOO and UGT unions under the banner “wages, housing and prices”, which drew at least 120,000 marchers in Madrid and 55,000 in Barcelona according to the authorities, and many more according to the organisers, Euronews reports. Rents soared by 87% between 2015 and 2025 while wages rose by about 30%, according to El País, cited by Time, and the average rent swallows almost the entire average salary of 16- to 29-year-olds, according to Spain’s Youth Council. Police made at least 75 arrests, the leader of the People’s Party, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, denounced a strike aimed at the opposition, and polls make the right favourite to win the snap election that the prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, has called for 29 November.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: In South Sudan, Amnesty accuses the UN and Juba of ignoring warnings before a massacre
items.content_html:
The rights group says the authorities and UN peacekeepers knew an attack was being prepared on Abiemnom, where at least 213 people were killed on 1 March. The report comes six weeks before the first elections since independence.

In a report published this week, Amnesty International says South Sudan’s government and the United Nations Mission in South Sudan had enough information and time to prevent the attack of 1 March on Abiemnom, near the Sudanese border, which killed at least 213 people according to the authorities. According to the group, which interviewed 82 people, between 1,000 and 1,500 gunmen from neighbouring Mayom county shot residents, destroyed more than 230 buildings and looted part of the hospital, while the UN mission reinforced its small garrison only once the assault was over. The mission blames resources squeezed by budget cuts, Juba did not respond to Amnesty, which wants an independent inquiry, and the country, whose president, Salva Kiir, dissolved the transitional government in September, is due to vote on 22 December for the first time since independence.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: After seeing Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump’s envoys head to Dublin to meet Volodymyr Zelensky
items.content_html:
Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner spent more than two hours at the Kremlin on Thursday, with nothing announced on the substance of the conflict. Moscow says they backed a humanitarian mission to Kostiantynivka.

On Thursday 12 November Russia’s president, Vladimir Putin, received America’s envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, at the Kremlin for more than two hours, a day after two days of three-way talks in Abu Dhabi ended in a prisoner-exchange deal, according to TASS and ABC News. The Kremlin’s foreign-policy adviser, Yuri Ushakov, called the meeting “constructive” and said the Americans supported a Russian proposal for a humanitarian mission to Kostiantynivka, in the Donetsk region, and that the three-way talks would continue, but said nothing on territory, which Moscow demands and Kyiv refuses to cede. The two envoys are expected in Dublin on Thursday evening to see Volodymyr Zelensky, who doubts they will bring back “something concrete”, while a Russian drone strike on a block of flats in Kyiv killed a woman and injured seven people that morning, according to Meduza and ABC News.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Israel is reportedly readying a strike on Iran as two supertankers explode in Hormuz
items.content_html:
Israel’s security cabinet has reportedly ordered the army to step up preparations for an attack, according to the public broadcaster Kan. In Hormuz, the Revolutionary Guards say two supertankers were disabled by explosions.

On the evening of Wednesday 11 November Israel’s security cabinet, chaired by the caretaker prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, ordered the army to step up preparations for an attack on Iran, according to the public broadcaster Kan, cited by Al Jazeera, even as Gadi Eisenkot urged him not to deploy the army without a direct and immediate threat. That same night two supertankers were disabled by explosions in the Strait of Hormuz after ignoring warnings, the Revolutionary Guards said on Thursday, threatening the same fate for any ship that co-operates with the American armed forces, according to Reuters. Donald Trump says he is ready to return to war if Qatar’s mediation fails, even though his secretary of state, Marco Rubio, thinks the blockade effective enough to make that unnecessary, and Brent closed at $92.76 on Wednesday after Tehran rejected moving its enriched uranium to a third country, according to Al Jazeera.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Ebola in DR Congo passes 11,000 confirmed cases and 5,300 deaths
items.content_html:
Figures published on Tuesday by the Congolese government confirm an outbreak of exceptional scale, the second-largest ever recorded. No vaccine or treatment is approved against the Bundibugyo strain.

According to figures published by the Congolese government on Tuesday 10 November, the Ebola outbreak declared in mid-May in the east of the Democratic Republic of Congo now stands at 11,042 confirmed cases and 5,387 deaths, the worst in the country’s history, Reuters and the AP report. Caused by the Bundibugyo strain, for which no vaccine or treatment has been approved, it has reached eight of the country’s 26 provinces, above all Ituri and North Kivu, where insecurity hampers access to treatment centres and many patients die at home, according to Reuters. It is the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record, after West Africa’s in 2014-2016, and the vaccine trial launched in Bunia at the end of October is not expected to produce results before 2027, while Kenya has recorded nine cases and Nigeria one imported case.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.
tags: The Ebola outbreak in DR Congo

items.title: At COP31, António Guterres urges world leaders to be done with fossil fuels
items.content_html:
Addressing the leaders’ summit in Antalya, the UN secretary-general said a temporary overshoot of 1.5°C was now inevitable. He wants an end to new coal, oil and gas projects.

On Wednesday 11 November, addressing the COP31 leaders’ summit in Antalya, Turkey, the UN secretary-general, António Guterres, said that overshooting the 1.5°C warming threshold was “now inevitable” and called for an end to all new coal, oil and gas projects. Global emissions would need to fall by about 6% a year, whereas national plans deliver a third of that at best and point to more than 2.5°C of warming by the end of the century, he said, before proposing a tax on oil companies’ windfall profits. Brazil’s president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, lamented that climate had vanished from G7 and G20 speeches, Iran’s Masoud Pezeshkian demanded compensation for the environmental damage done by wars, and the negotiations, led by Australia, are due to end on 20 November.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: In northern Tigray, Ethiopia’s army and Eritrean forces are reported to be clashing around Badme
items.content_html:
Having retaken most of Tigray in October, the federal army is pushing towards the Eritrean border. Addis Ababa accuses Asmara of invasion; Asmara calls that a pretext for war.

On Monday 9 November Ethiopia’s federal army and Eritrean forces reportedly clashed around Badme, a long-disputed border town, according to observers cited by the Critical Threats Project, which could not confirm it, after the Ethiopian army took Sheraro and Adi Awala on 3 November. Since late September federal troops, allied with a breakaway Tigrayan faction, have been fighting the forces of the Tigray People’s Liberation Front, and Addis Ababa accuses Eritrea of an “invasion” reaching 60km into Tigray, which Asmara portrays as a pretext for a war of aggression. The prime minister, Abiy Ahmed, who regards his country’s access to the Red Sea as inevitable, installed an interim government in Tigray in mid-October, while Chinese envoys were received in Addis Ababa in early November and then by Eritrea’s president, Isaias Afwerki, in an effort to avert open war.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Russia and Ukraine agree a vast prisoner exchange in Abu Dhabi, but no breakthrough
items.content_html:
The American-brokered talks ended on Wednesday with an agreement in principle covering more than 1,000 prisoners on each side, according to Moscow. Nothing moved on territory, and America’s envoys are expected at the Kremlin on Thursday.

On Wednesday 11 November, after a second session of under two hours in Abu Dhabi, Russia and Ukraine announced an agreement in principle on a large prisoner exchange, which the Russian general Alexander Zorin says will be the biggest of the war, with more than 1,000 people on each side, according to TASS. Ukraine’s chief negotiator, Rustem Umerov, called the swap the “main result” of the talks, but nothing moved on territory: Russia’s negotiator, Vladimir Medinsky, repeated that Moscow would recover “every inch” of the land it claims, while Kyiv still insists on a ceasefire first. The American envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff are due to meet Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Thursday and then Volodymyr Zelensky in Dublin, and the exchange, whose numbers are to be settled on Thursday, could take place within two or three weeks, the Russian side told the AP.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: France accuses Iran’s Revolutionary Guards of sabotaging the fridges of 700 shops
items.content_html:
France’s foreign minister blames a cyber unit linked to the Guards for the attack on supermarkets on 12 October. Iran’s ambassador has been summoned and Paris wants European sanctions.

On Monday 9 November France’s foreign minister, Jean-Noël Barrot, blamed Iran’s Revolutionary Guards for the cyber-attack which, on the night of 11-12 October, tampered with refrigeration in some 700 French shops, including Carrefour, Monoprix, Intermarché and Coopérative U stores. According to ANSSI, France’s national cyber-security agency, the attack was the work of Shahid Kaveh, a unit linked to the Guards and betrayed by traces of Persian and Iranian IP addresses, and temperatures rose as high as 50°C for about six hours, the AP reports. Paris has summoned Iran’s ambassador and wants European sanctions, which EU foreign ministers could discuss on 16 November, while Tehran dismisses the accusations as “baseless and biased”.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Indonesia’s vice-president, Gibran Rakabuming Raka, resigns amid doubts over his diplomas
items.content_html:
The son of the former president Joko Widodo handed his resignation to President Prabowo Subianto on Wednesday, after court rulings found his school qualifications wanting. Parliament will then have 60 days to elect a successor.

On Wednesday 11 November Indonesia’s vice-president, Gibran Rakabuming Raka, handed his resignation to President Prabowo Subianto at a meeting at Halim Perdanakusuma air base in Jakarta, his ally Budi Arie Setiadi, chairman of the Projo organisation, confirmed to Reuters and the Antara news agency. The son of the former president Joko Widodo had been under pressure since the Constitutional Court and then the Supreme Court ruled that his studies abroad did not meet the requirements for his candidacy in 2024, and 120 legislators had just filed a petition demanding his impeachment. According to the senior law minister, Yusril Ihza Mahendra, Parliament must declare the post vacant and then, within 60 days, elect a successor from two names put forward by the president, an uncertainty that is weighing on investor confidence, Reuters notes.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: In Haiti, Salvadoran troops destroy the house of the 400 Mawozo gang’s leader
items.content_html:
El Salvador’s president, Nayib Bukele, on Tuesday claimed the assault on the gang’s headquarters in Croix-des-Bouquets, where its leader was absent. American diplomats complain that El Salvador is acting without co-ordinating with the UN-backed force.

At around 2.30am on Sunday 8 November a drone unit of the Haitian police, backed by Salvadoran soldiers and helicopters, destroyed the house of Wilson Joseph, leader of the 400 Mawozo gang, in Croix-des-Bouquets near Port-au-Prince, described as his headquarters. El Salvador’s president, Nayib Bukele, who had vowed to raze the house, claimed the operation on Tuesday; it reportedly left about 20 dead according to the Miami Herald, a toll AFP could not confirm, and Wilson Joseph was absent, according to the Salvadoran press. Haiti’s prime minister, Alix Didier Fils-Aimé, praised El Salvador, but American diplomats complain that the 2,000 or so Salvadoran soldiers, most of them outside the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force, are not co-ordinating with it, according to Axios.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Niger has taken in nearly 64,000 refugees from Nigeria since January, says the UNHCR
items.content_html:
Jihadist and criminal violence in northern Nigeria is driving tens of thousands of people into a drought-stricken neighbour. For lack of money, only 5% of the new arrivals have been registered.

On Tuesday 10 November the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) said that nearly 64,000 people had fled northern Nigeria for Niger since the start of the year, and several hundred more for Benin, driven out by Boko Haram, Islamic State West Africa and criminal gangs. Most settle in the border regions of Diffa, which accounts for more than 70% of the security incidents recorded in Niger this year, and Tahoua, where they lack food, water and shelter, while malnutrition and respiratory infections are spreading. The UNHCR is appealing for $11.4m for Niger, Nigeria and Benin, at a time when Niger was already hosting more than 500,000 refugees and asylum-seekers and drought threatens the harvests of some 700 of the region’s 1,000 villages.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: In Abu Dhabi, Russians, Ukrainians and Americans reopen talks, with Europeans kept in the wings
items.content_html:
Delegations from the three countries meet on Tuesday and Wednesday in the United Arab Emirates, together for the first time since February. The Europeans will be on hand, but Moscow refuses to let them join talks focused on security.

Two days of talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States, represented by the envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, open in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday 10 November, the first three-way meeting since February, when the war with Iran pulled Washington’s attention away. Moscow still demands that Ukraine withdraw from the Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions and give up on NATO, while Kyiv refuses to cede territory Russia has not conquered and wants a ceasefire first, so none of the analysts consulted by Al Jazeera expects a peace deal. A European team led by Björn Seibert, Ursula von der Leyen’s chief of staff, along with French, German and British advisers, will be present, but the Kremlin insists they will not take part in the talks, which Sergei Lavrov says will open with security.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Kraków’s Market Square gunman dies as terrorism investigators look for possible accomplices
items.content_html:
The man behind Saturday’s shooting, which killed six people in the city’s historic heart, died in hospital on Monday. Prosecutors, who are treating it as terrorism, are now cautious about his ideological motives.

At 4.30am on Monday 9 November the 24-year-old Pole who had opened fire from his car on Kraków’s Market Square at around 3pm on Saturday, killing six people and wounding fifteen, died in hospital, the police announced. The dead include four Poles, a Briton and an Austrian woman, and the bodies of the gunman’s father, mother and sister were found at the family home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, some 150 kilometres to the north-east. The national prosecutor’s office, which has opened a terrorism investigation, is trying to establish whether others inspired or helped the attacker, as Poland emerges from two days of national mourning and celebrates its independence day on Wednesday.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Nvidia investigates its boss, Jensen Huang, over ties to a woman suspected of spying for Beijing
items.content_html:
The board of the AI-chip giant has handed an inquiry to independent directors after its chief executive’s admission. Three House committee chairmen want to question him behind closed doors.

On Sunday 8 November Nvidia’s board announced an investigation by a committee of independent directors, assisted by outside lawyers, after its chief executive, Jensen Huang, admitted an intimate relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data-centre company. According to the New York Times, American intelligence concluded that she was passing information to Beijing, which China dismisses as baseless speculation, and a Malaysian company linked to Megaspeed bought at least $4.8bn of equipment built on Nvidia technology. The board says it has no reason to believe that national security or confidential information was compromised and retains confidence in its boss, whom three House committee chairmen want to question in a closed-door session on 18 November.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.
tags: Nvidia and the China spying claims

items.title: South Africa’s ANC suffers its worst setback as the big cities hunt for coalitions
items.content_html:
Nelson Mandela’s party won only about 31% of the vote in the local elections of 4 November, ahead of the Democratic Alliance. With no majority, several big cities, including Pretoria and Durban, will have to be run by coalitions.

With 99% of ballots counted in the local elections of 4 November, the African National Congress (ANC) had 30.8% of the vote, down from 45.6% in 2021, and the Democratic Alliance (DA) 24%, according to the chairman of the electoral commission, Mosotho Moepya. The ANC’s secretary-general, Fikile Mbalula, called the result “catastrophic”, while Jacob Zuma’s uMkhonto we Sizwe party, third with nearly 10%, came first in Durban, and the Economic Freedom Fighters slipped to 6.2%. Cape Town gave the DA an outright majority, but Pretoria and Durban remain hung, and the bargaining begins little more than a year before the ANC conference that is due, in December 2027, to choose Cyril Ramaphosa’s successor as party leader.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: In Yemen, at least 30 killed at a market near Taiz, with each side blaming the other
items.content_html:
The Houthis accuse Saudi aircraft of bombing the Al-Hadara market on Friday; the recognised government blames Houthi missiles. According to the Yemen Data Project, October was the deadliest month for civilians since 2017.

At around 7am on Friday 6 November strikes hit the Al-Hadara market in the Al-Waziyah district of Taiz province, killing at least 30 people and wounding eight, according to the Houthi authorities, a toll the Associated Press could not verify. The Houthis’ military spokesman, Yahya Saree, blames Saudi aircraft, while the spokesman for government forces, Colonel Majed al-Nazili, attributes the carnage to Houthi ballistic missiles and calls it a “war crime”. The attack is part of an escalation that began in July with the collapse of the UN-brokered truce, as the Houthis have besieged the city of Taiz for a month and the government’s “Dawn of Yemen” offensive, launched on 5 October, grinds on.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Gadi Eisenkot accepts the mandate in Israel and calls for a national emergency government
items.content_html:
The former army chief was formally asked on Sunday to form a government, with 67 recommendations but a bloc of only 48 members. He has invited Likud to join him and set four conditions for any partner.

On Sunday 8 November, at the presidential residence in Jerusalem, Israel’s president, Isaac Herzog, formally handed Gadi Eisenkot, the leader of the Yashar party, the mandate to form the next government, a day after announcing his choice. Recommended by 67 of the Knesset’s 120 members, against 46 for Benjamin Netanyahu, the former chief of staff commands a bloc of only 48 and has promised creative, unconventional political moves to build a national emergency government. He has until 6 December, extendable to 20 December, to assemble a majority, while the new members are due to be sworn in on Tuesday and Mr Netanyahu stays on as caretaker prime minister.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Houthi attack damages an Aramco tower in the heart of Riyadh’s financial district
items.content_html:
Missiles fired from Yemen were intercepted over the Saudi capital on Sunday, but debris struck a building belonging to the oil giant. The Houthi authorities accuse Saudi aircraft of killing dozens of people near Sanaa.

Overnight on Saturday 7 and Sunday 8 November Saudi air defences intercepted Houthi missiles fired at Riyadh, but debris blew out the windows of several floors of an Aramco building in the King Abdullah Financial District, causing no casualties, according to the energy ministry. The Iran-aligned Yemeni rebels have stepped up their fire on the kingdom’s ports and airports since September, and their spokesman, Yahya Saree, claims they also targeted Riyadh’s international airport, which the Saudi authorities have not confirmed. The Saudi-led coalition says it destroyed missile launchers in Saada and Sanaa, while the Houthi-run health ministry reports at least 33 people killed on Saturday and 40 on Sunday in Saudi strikes near the Yemeni capital.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: In Ukraine 850,000 people lose power ahead of the talks in Abu Dhabi
items.content_html:
Fresh Russian strikes hit the power grid on Sunday, notably in the Dnipropetrovsk region, and the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant lost its external power supply. Paris says Europeans will take part in the talks on 10 and 11 November.

Overnight Russian strikes on Sunday 8 November left more than 850,000 people in Ukraine without electricity, over 600,000 of them in the Dnipropetrovsk region, according to the energy company DTEK, while one person was killed and three wounded in Dnipro. The Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant lost its external power and is running on diesel generators, and a drone hit the site in Komyshuvakha where an earlier strike killed at least 55 people, targeting rescuers, according to Kyiv. France’s foreign minister, Jean-Noël Barrot, announced that France and other Europeans would join the talks in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November, which had until now been conceived as a meeting between Washington, Moscow and Kyiv.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: COP31 opens in Antalya as the world looks set to overshoot 1.5°C
items.content_html:
Nearly 200 countries meet in Turkey until 20 November for the UN climate conference, presided over by Ankara with Australia leading the negotiations. Current policies point to 2.8°C of warming, according to the UN’s latest projection.

The 31st UN climate conference opens on Monday 9 November in Antalya, Turkey, bringing together delegations from nearly 200 countries until 20 November under the presidency of Turkey’s environment minister, Murat Kurum. Scientists consider it almost certain that warming will exceed 1.5°C in 2026, and current policies point to a rise of 2.8°C by the end of the century, according to the UN’s latest projection, cited by the German news agency DPA. Australia’s climate minister, Chris Bowen, will chair the negotiations, an unprecedented division of roles, ahead of a leaders’ summit on 11 and 12 November at which markedly fewer heads of state are expected than at recent COPs.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Myanmar’s army kills eleven people in an air strike on a school in Sagaing
items.content_html:
Teachers and children were among the victims of a bombing on Saturday in Kani township, according to independent Burmese media. The National Unity Government counted 641 army air strikes in October.

At around 11.30am on Saturday 7 November an air strike by Myanmar’s army hit a school and the village of Nyaung Pin Le, in Kani township in the Sagaing region, killing eleven people, most of them teachers and children, according to independent media. The bombing is part of an air campaign that killed 212 civilians in October, 23 of them children, according to the exiled National Unity Government, nearly six years after the coup and seven months after Min Aung Hlaing was elected president. Fighting continues in Mon State, where more than 15,000 residents have fled Kyaikto township, and in Rakhine, while from 9 November the army is closing checkpoints at night in three Sagaing townships.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Isaac Herzog asks Gadi Eisenkot, not Benjamin Netanyahu, to form Israel’s next government
items.content_html:
On Saturday evening Israel’s president gave the leader of Yashar, backed by 67 members of the Knesset, the job of building a coalition. Benjamin Netanyahu accuses his rival of wanting to govern with “supporters of terrorism”.

On the evening of Saturday 7 November Israel’s president, Isaac Herzog, announced that he would ask Gadi Eisenkot, a former chief of staff who leads the Yashar party, to form the next government, with the mandate to be handed over formally on Sunday at the presidential residence in Jerusalem. The former general was recommended by 67 of the Knesset’s 120 members, including the Arab parties, against 46 for Benjamin Netanyahu, but his own bloc holds only 48 seats and several of his allies refuse to depend on Ra’am and the United List. Mr Eisenkot has 28 days, extendable by 14, to muster at least 61 members, while the outgoing prime minister is calling for a “national unity government” that would include his far-right allies and the ultra-Orthodox parties.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Iran lifts the range limit on its missiles after fresh American strikes in Hormuz
items.content_html:
The Revolutionary Guards say they no longer observe a 2,000km ceiling on their ballistic missiles. Washington has set up a force to hunt down Iranian arms smuggling, as advisers urge Donald Trump to resume the war.

On Saturday 7 November the spokesman for the Revolutionary Guards, General Hossein Mohebbi, said in Tehran that the 2,000km limit Iran had imposed on the range of its ballistic missiles had been lifted, a day after American strikes on air defences on Qeshm island. The announcement, which does not say whether Iran already has longer-range missiles, came alongside a statement attributed to the Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, promising a response “without geographical limits” to any American or Israeli threat. According to NBC, advisers have urged Donald Trump to resume large-scale operations before the new Congress sits in January, and America’s Central Command has announced a force to cut the land and Caspian routes by which Iran obtains weapons.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Russia fires 36 ballistic missiles at Kyiv three days before talks in Abu Dhabi
items.content_html:
Overnight on 6-7 November Russia targeted the capital’s power grid and damaged the North Bridge over the Dnipro. Volodymyr Zelensky accuses Moscow of preparing for negotiations “by launching ballistic missiles”.

Overnight on Friday 6 and Saturday 7 November Russia fired 36 ballistic missiles at Kyiv and its region, only four of which were shot down for want of Patriot interceptors, according to President Volodymyr Zelensky, along with 172 drones across 13 regions, wounding at least nine people, including a child. The strikes hit the substations linking the Rivne and Khmelnytskyi nuclear plants to the capital, leaving parts of the city without electricity, heating and water, and damaged the North Bridge, which Moscow says it was aiming at. Ukrainian, Russian and American delegations are due to meet in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday 10 November for a fourth round of talks brokered by Washington, as the death toll from the strike on Komyshuvakha, in the Zaporizhzhia region, reaches 55.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Hoax bomb threats spread to European newsrooms after targeting dozens of flights
items.content_html:
Ireland’s public broadcaster, RTÉ, evacuated its offices on Friday after a threatening email, as did Bulgaria’s Nova TV. Nearly 30 flights have been targeted since Tuesday, and no explosives have been found.

On Friday 6 November emails signed by one “Mikhail Andropov” and headed “Message to the West” threatened Ireland’s public broadcaster, RTÉ, which evacuated its offices and suspended programming, as well as Bulgaria’s Nova TV, while Sky reported a threat in Britain.
